Because the Crow Tribe has first option to buy the land after reclamation, they should be vitally interested in the level of restoration which will be practiced on the mined lands. If long term stability and productivity is not built into the land during reclamation (when equipment and money is available, if needed, for alternative techniques) it is very unlikely that the Tribe will be able to afford corrective measures later, when short-comings of proposed reclamation techniques may become apparent. At present, the reliability of proposed reclamation techniques cannot be guaranteed; consequently, the Tribe may wish to pay very close attention to the results obtained.
The Tribe may also have other ideas about how they might wish to use the reclaimed lands. If so, they should make their wishes known during planning phases, so that needed techniques can be selected for reclamation operations.
Fish and Wildlife Habitat
Fish and wildlife would benefit most directly if reclamation were specifically designed to provide suitable primary or secondary habitat. Creation of new or restored habitat would allow increased numbers of selected species, or increased general species diversity, depending upon the reclamation design selected by the company and the future land owners.
